idea-plugin.name: JenkSpotter
idea-plugin.description:
Keep an eye on your Jenkins builds while you keep working: get notified when they finish or wait for your approval, and start, rebuild, abort and read them without leaving the IDE.

Built for big Jenkins installations: hundreds of jobs in folders and multibranch pipelines, several servers, and a lot of builds that are none of your business.

Main features

  • Builds you care about – builds you started anywhere (browser, CLI, IDE), pinned and watched jobs, Jenkins views and the builds of the branch checked out in the project. Follow-up builds are nested below the build that started them
  • Notifications – when a build finishes, with sounds, an OS notification while the IDE is in the background and a status bar widget. A pipeline waiting for an input step can be answered or aborted right from the notification
  • Why a build failed – rest the mouse on a failed build to see the failed stage, the failed tests and the error lines of the log; errors are highlighted in the live console log and F2 jumps between them
  • Build details – overview, stages (nested and parallel), failed tests (go to the test, run it locally), changes, artifacts and the live console log
  • Find any job – fuzzy search over all jobs including folders and multibranch pipelines from anywhere with Go to Jenkins Job (Cmd+Alt+Shift+J on macOS, Ctrl+Alt+Shift+K on Windows/Linux); paste a Jenkins URL to pin that job
  • Build with parameters – string, text, boolean, choice, password, Active Choices, credentials and run parameters. Values are remembered per job, Rebuild reuses the previous ones
  • Call graph – which jobs trigger a job and what it triggers, as a graph, a tree or complete paths; copy it as a Mermaid diagram
  • Filters – status chips, regular expressions (with a builder), a folder tree and This project cut a big Jenkins down to what matters to you
  • Several Jenkins servers – each with its own user name and API token, with a connection light per server

Getting started

  1. Create an API token in Jenkins under your user | Security | API Token.
  2. Add your Jenkins in Settings | Tools | JenkSpotter with your user name and the token. Test Connection shows under which user Jenkins knows you.
  3. Open the JenkSpotter tool window.

Optional Jenkins plugins that unlock more details: Pipeline: Stage View or Pipeline Graph View (stages; nested and parallel ones need Pipeline Graph View), JUnit (failed tests), Blue Ocean (to open builds there).

Privacy

JenkSpotter does not collect or transmit any data. It only connects to the Jenkins servers you configure, using the IDE's proxy and certificate settings. API tokens are kept in the IDE password safe, never in a settings file.

Feedback

Found a bug or have an idea? Open an issue on GitHub.
